goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check bypassed for bookings with no eventType team: team queries called with teamId ?? 0 and check relies only on isOrganizer/isAttendee (addGuests.handler.ts:43-49)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the authorization gate is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`. Even when `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` yields 0, that only affects `isTeamAdminOrOwner` (and would typically make it false), but it does not bypass auth—access is still restricted to the organizer (`booking.userId === user.id`) or an existing attendee (`booking.attendees.find(...)`). If anything, passing `0` could incorrectly *deny* team admins/owners for bookings lacking a teamId, not allow unauthorized users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking lookup findFirst({ where: { id } }) is not scoped to the requester's team/user before loading organizer details and credentials (addGuests.handler.ts:43-49)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler first loads a booking via `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { ... user: { include: { credentials: true }}}})` without scoping it to the requester (e.g., organizer/team membership) before performing the permission check. This allows booking existence enumeration (`NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN`) and unnecessarily loads organizer/user credential-related data for unauthorized requests before rejecting them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation of booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings and confirmation emails/ICS REQUEST sent (addGuests.handler.ts:35-41)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to update `attendees`, call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` without checking any `booking.status` (e.g., cancelled/rejected). The diff shows no guard preventing guest addition (and resulting emails/ICS REQUEST updates) for non-active bookings, which would be incorrect behavior if such statuses exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: new EventManager({ ...user, credentials }) uses current session user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so calendar update fails or misses organizer's calendar when an attendee adds guests (addGuests.handler.ts:160-163)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is the current session user (could be an attendee) rather than the booking organizer (`booking.userId` / `organizer` fetched earlier). Since `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` likely needs the organizer’s calendar credentials to update the event on the organizer/destination calendar, using the attendee’s credentials can cause the update to fail or not affect the organizer’s calendar when a non-organizer adds guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is swallowed with console.log only, error object discarded and user still sees success toast (addGuests.handler.ts:170-172)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the email sending is wrapped in a try/catch that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards `err`, then the handler still returns success (`{ message: "Guests added" }`). This means email delivery failures are not observable/traceable and the client mutation will still hit `onSuccess` and show the success toast, even if emails failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or when user edits emails; error banner persists until Cancel (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:29-50)

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd`, but it is not cleared in the mutation `onSuccess` (only `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])` are called). It is also not cleared when the user edits email inputs via `MultiEmail` (`setMultiEmailValue` is passed directly with no reset). Therefore the error banner can persist across edits and even after a successful add when the dialog is reopened (only Cancel resets it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast does t(err.message), which renders raw strings for non-key messages and shows raw error codes via err.data?.code to end users (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38)

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds a toast message as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. This will surface internal TRPC error codes like `BAD_REQUEST`/`FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND` to end users, and it assumes `err.message` is always a translation key (otherwise `t(err.message)` will likely display the raw string). This is a concrete UX/message-handling issue in the diff, but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: List items keyed by array index in MultiEmail.tsx:31, which can cause stale input state when removing an email from the middle

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders `value.map((field, index) => ( <li key={index}> ... ))`. Since emails can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`, removing an item from the middle shifts subsequent indices/keys, which can cause React to reuse the wrong component instances (e.g., focus/validation/internal state in `EmailField`) and lead to stale/mismatched input state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Translation promises re-created for every attendee on each add and sendAddGuestsEmails emails all attendees on every add, scaling O(existing guests) per invocation (addGuests.handler.ts:98-115)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` maps over **all** `bookingAttendees.attendees` and calls `getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` per attendee (roughly lines 98-115 in the new file), which will re-run translation loading for every attendee on each mutation invocation. Separately, `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` iterates `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` and sends an email for each attendee on every add, so work/email volume scales with existing attendee count. This is a verifiable perf/scaling concern introduced by the diff, not an outright functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails newGuests matching is case-sensitive against attendee.email, so new guests may receive the guests-added notification instead of the booking confirmation ICS; also lacks blank-line separation style of sibling exports (email-manager.ts:525)

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` does a case-sensitive exact-string match. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `toLowerCase()`) of either `newGuests` or `attendee.email`, so if attendee emails are stored/canonicalized with different casing than the input array, a newly added guest could fail the check and incorrectly receive `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` instead of `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. The note about blank-line separation is merely a style nit, but the case-sensitive matching is a behavior/correctness issue grounded in the diff.
